title: Cross-region warm-standby capacity plan (Apr 2026)
body:
Purpose:
Provide a compact, operationally-actionable warm-standby capacity plan and activation runbook for multi-region GPU fleet failover. This sheet captures sizing targets, triggers, cost delta, and the SRE playbook to ramp standby capacity with minimal impact to tail latency.

Executive summary:
- Design: maintain a small always-resident "warm" pool in each region: pre-provisioned VMs/GPU with models pre-loaded and KV cache primed to allow serving within 60-120s when promoted to hot.
- Goal SLOs on failover: no more than 2x request latency increase for 95th pctile, and <2% request loss during activation windows for region-total outages.
- Target fleet warm buffer: 7-10% of region usable GPUs (tunable by region).
- Expected monthly cost increase: ~15% of infra spend for warm standby (example calc below).

Assumptions and definitions:
- Usable GPU = GPUs available for production model slices (after reserved infra and infra maintenance buffers).
- Warm standby = active VMs with GPU, container running model process in paused/standby state; traffic disabled in router but health probes allowed. Warm -> hot promotion includes enabling route, warming KV cache with live traffic replay or warm-up shards. Promotion time target = 60-120s.
- Cold standby = image snapshots + instance templates, target promotion 10+ minutes. Not covered here.

Current fleet snapshot (Apr 2026):
Region | GPUs_total | baseline_util_avg | notes
US-WEST-2 | 140 | 0.61 | primary west coast; many low-latency customers
US-EAST-1 | 120 | 0.65 | east coast traffic; maintenance window Fri 02:00-06:00 UTC
EU-WEST-1 | 90  | 0.58 | European customers; regional data locality requirements
AP-SOUTHEAST-1 | 70  | 0.54 | Asia-Pacific growth region (spikey)
Global total | 420 | fleet_avg 0.60 | 

Warm standby sizing proposal (region-level):
Region | GPUs_total | warm_target_pct | warm_gpus (rounded) | rationale
US-WEST-2 | 140 | 8% | 11 | high-traffic; want quick absorption for west outages
US-EAST-1 | 120 | 9% | 11 | east handles broad traffic; slightly larger buffer
EU-WEST-1 | 90  | 7% | 6  | lower burst profile but regulatory routing needs
AP-SOUTHEAST-1 | 70  | 10% | 7  | high growth + higher outage risk from interconnects
Fleet total warm GPUs target = 35 (≈8.3% of total)

Cost estimate (example):
- Baseline monthly infra bill (GPU infra only): $400k
- Warm standby incremental (35 GPUs reserved) approx 35/420 =~ 8.3% extra capacity. With instance-hour costs and reserved discounts, ballpark cost delta ≈ 12–18% depending on reserved pricing. We estimate +$60k/month.
- Note: warm pools can be rightsized with spot-backed burst lanes to reduce incremental spend during normal operation.

Activation triggers and policy (operator-facing):
1) Immediate region outage (region BGP / cloud zone degraded):
   - Auto-detect: cloud provider region health alert OR global router signals >30% route failures to region for >30s.
   - Action: start cross-region promotion: route policy = latency-first for user-facing routes; cost-first fallback only for non-latency-sensitive background jobs.
   - Promote warm pools in other regions up to 50% of their warm size instantly, then iterate based on observed latency.
2) Capacity pressure (sustained high utilization):
   - Auto-detect: region usable capacity utilization >78% sustained for 2 min OR request throttling >1% for 1 min.
   - Action: ramp warm pool by converting queued warm nodes to hot via rfctl promote commands (see runbook). If warm pool exhausted, trigger cross-region spillover with traffic shaping.
3) Gradual degraded performance (latency increases):
   - Auto-detect: 95p latency > baseline*2 for 3 consecutive 1-min windows.
   - Action: pre-warm model shards by injecting synthetic warmup traffic to standby nodes, enable app-level fallback to quantized variant (reduce approx +30% throughput), and enable carved A/B routing to minimize customer impact.

Routing and traffic policies:
- Router rules: priority order = local_hot -> local_warm (after promotion) -> regional_fallback (nearest healthy region) -> global_fallback (quantized models).
- Throttle policy during failover: token-bucket qps caps per org to preserve tail latency until full promotion completes. Default burst-per-org = 3x baseline for 120s.
- Consistency: for sessions that require region-local data, honor data locality routes; for others, route to nearest healthy region.

Warm promotion runbook (SRE checklist):
1) Confirm alert and scope: identify affected region(s), check cloud provider status page, and announce incident channel.
2) Run capacity check: rfctl pool-status --region=<region> to view warm_avail, warm_inflight, total_hot
3) Promote warm nodes: rfctl promote --pool warm-<region> --count <n> --reason "failover-<incident-id>". Example: rfctl promote --pool warm-us-west-2 --count 8 --reason failover-2026-04-09-01
4) Warm KV cache: kick off kv-warm --targets <promoted-nodes> --model <model-id> (automated; watch progress in /ops/kv-warm). Target warm rate = 80% in 90s.
5) Adjust routing: enable warm node endpoint group in global-router; monitor latency, error rate.
6) If warm pool insufficient: rfctl scale --pool burst-cross-region --count <n> to spin on-demand instances in secondary regions (spot-backed where allowed).
7) After steady-state: reduce throttle restrictions gradually and revert traffic shaping.
8) Post-incident: mark promoted warm nodes for diagnostics (rfctl annotate), capture KV warm logs, and run failure-after-action (postmortem).

Operational notes and mitigations:
- Pre-warm cadence: schedule a daily short warm-kv ping to top 30% busiest standby nodes to keep model I/O caches warm and detect silent failures.
- Maintenance windows: reduce warm_target_pct by 50% in controlled maintenance windows only after acceptance by on-call.
- Hot-swap testing: run quarterly simulated region-failover drills that execute the runbook end-to-end with canary traffic. Track mean time to full promotion (goal < 180s).
- Cost optimization: where permissible, use spot-backed warm nodes with automated fallback to reserved warm nodes if spot preemption frequency > threshold.

Metrics to capture for ongoing tuning:
- promotion_time_seconds (median / 95p)
- warm_utilization_ratio = hot_serving_tokens_on_promoted_nodes / promoted_node_capacity
- failover_lost_requests_pct during window
- incremental_cost_per_promoted_gpu_hour

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Final warm_target_pct per region: confirm with product for EU data locality impact (PRIO: high).
- Which models are allowed to have quantized fallback during failover (safety & quality tradeoffs).
- SLAs for customers on dedicated pools vs hosted: should warm standby be billed differently?

Appendix: quick-size calculations
- Example promotion capacity needed for full west outage: assume US-WEST-2 (140 GPUs) traffic is redistributed to other regions. If US-WEST-2 is 33% of fleet, to absorb 100% of its traffic we need roughly 140 * 1.0 = 140 extra GPU-equivalents across other regions. Warm pools cover ~35 GPUs. Additional absorption plan: combine warm pools (35) + burst-on-demand (spot/reserved) scaled to 105 GPUs across prioritized regions.
- Quick math: incremental hours for 105 GPUs * 24 * 30 = 75,600 gpu-hours. At effective cost $0.85 per gpu-hour = ~$64k incremental for a month-long full-failover scenario (worst case).

Contact and ownership:
- Draft owner: Maya Patel (infrastructure capacity)
- Secondary: Diego Ramos (SRE lead), Lina Zhang (cost ops)
- Review cadence: weekly until policy stabilized, then monthly.

Last updated: 2026-04-12 by Maya Patel.

Notes to reviewers (scratchpad):
- Consider adjusting APAC warm_target to 12% given growth forecasts from product; run a simulation using the weekend traffic spike dataset.
- Need a CI job to validate rfctl promote dry-run path so dry-run exposes missing IAM roles before on-call runs actual promotion.

(End of sheet)
